name: matching-cu-comparison
description: Compare the compute-unit cost of two orderbook implementations on the same matching workload: the deliberately-simple flat-array OrderBook and the critbit-tree Slab. The flat OrderBook is O(N) per fill — it exposes how Solana's per-instruction CU budget (default 200K) constrains DEX design at scale. The Slab amortizes to O(log N). Both are valid on-chain implementations; the gap is exactly what Solana's compute model rewards. Use this scenario when evaluating which data structure to use on your own market.
headline: Same matching workload, two orderbook backends. Flat O(N) vs critbit O(log N) measured in CUs.

steps.explanation: Boot the flat-array OrderBook and place 16 resting maker orders on each side.
Cross with a market order; measure CUs consumed. The match-cli surfaces the CU cost on stdout.
Repeat the workload against the critbit Slab. Compare its CU output against match-cli's.
Run the dedicated CU instrumentation harness for finer-grained measurements.
